# Activity, notifications and reporting API

Read routes require insight:read. Owned read/unread, watch, preferences and digest mutations require insight:write plus current organization/project visibility.

All endpoints use /api/v1 and the current people permission service. Cookie mutations require X-Crew-Request: 1. Personal inboxes, subscriptions, preferences and digests always belong to the authenticated account; no supplied userId changes that ownership. Token scopes and live project grants both apply. Lists use limit/cursor and filter inaccessible projects before pagination.

GET /activity requires orgId and insight:read. Optional projectId, issueId, userId (actor), entityType, action, from and to select a feed. Dates are ISO timestamps. Events include sanitized before/after fields and canonical issue keys. Arbitrary payloads, token/session credentials, invitation links and reset links are excluded. Organization activity is withheld from guests; their feed contains only explicitly granted projects. Cross-project relations require access to both issues.

GET /subscriptions lists the caller's accessible watches. POST {targetType:issue|project,targetId} starts or resumes a watch. DELETE /subscriptions/:targetType/:targetId mutes that target, including future automatic watcher subscriptions. Issue creators, assignees and mentioned users subscribe automatically. The actor receives no notification for their own action. Explicit mentions deliver a mention notification even when ordinary watching is muted.

GET /notifications accepts orgId,projectId,state=all|unread|read and pagination. It includes unread count after visibility filtering. PATCH /notifications/:id {read:true|false} updates one owned visible item. POST /notifications/mark accepts either ids or all:true, optional orgId, and read:boolean. Invalid ownership is rejected atomically. GET/PATCH /notification-preferences use orgId and emailEnabled/mentionsOnly booleans.

POST /digests {orgId} batches up to 200 unread, previously undigested visible notifications into the existing people outbox using kind=digest. The response includes count and remaining; repeat deliberately while remaining is positive. Batching preserves unread state and each notification enters a digest once. Email preferences can disable batching. GET /digests lists only the caller's digest messages and reconstructs their entries through current project access, never invitation/reset messages. The local shared outbox is the delivery surface; no external SMTP service is configured.

GET /events streams Server-Sent Events with optional orgId/projectId. Frames are ready, activity, heartbeat and reset. Activity IDs support Last-Event-ID replay of a recent bounded window; reset asks the client to refresh the feed. Current credentials, token scopes, membership and project grants are checked at every delivery and heartbeat. Revoked credentials close the connection. Slow clients are disconnected instead of retaining an unbounded event queue. Application cleanup removes listeners, clears heartbeat timers and ends all streams. Activity pages visibly refresh from live events and provide pause/resume and connection state.

The Activity page supports organization/project/issue/actor/entity/action/date filters, cursor navigation, field comparisons and manual refresh. Search and saved filters are documented in api-insight-search.md. Dashboard and transfer contracts follow.

## Dashboard

GET /dashboard?orgId=ID accepts projectId,weeks=1..52,date=YYYY-MM-DD,sprintId. GET /projects/:projectId/dashboard resolves organization automatically. insight:read scope plus current organization/project visibility apply before counts, assignee names, status groups, throughput or sprint selection. Counts are current issue totals (including zero workflow statuses); the optional date sets the UTC overdue/throughput reference and does not reconstruct historical counts. Weekly throughput counts distinct issue completion transitions per UTC Monday week, once per issue/week; null estimates contribute zero points. Sprint data reuses getBurndown and its persisted immutable work ledger. Future actuals remain null.

The Dashboard page provides organization/project/date/week and sprint selectors, issues/points units, actual SVG count/throughput/burndown charts, ideal/scope toggles, accessible chart data tables and live refresh. crew dashboard [show] --org ID [--project ID] [--weeks N] [--date DATE] [--sprint ID] prints the same authorized report.

## Project transfer version 1

GET /projects/:projectId/export?format=json|csv requires export:read on the source project. JSON is a streamed self-contained crew.project/version1 document with project/workflow/user catalogs, issues, labels, comments and relations. Relations to accessible external issues include an externalIssues catalog; inaccessible relation endpoints are excluded before export. CSV streams issue rows, doubles embedded quotes, retains multiline content and prefixes potential spreadsheet formulas (including leading whitespace) with an apostrophe. Attachment blobs, sprint history, watch state and notification state are excluded by the documented format. Back up CREW_DATA_DIR separately for full service state.

POST /orgs/:orgId/import accepts {document,key,name,userMap,externalIssueMap,preview}. It requires import:write, project:manage, issue:write and comment:write scopes with current organization management authority. preview:true validates the complete document and returns counts, resolved mappings and limitations without writing. Unknown fields/versions, duplicate IDs/numbers/labels/relations, malformed dates, orphan references, parent cycles and directed relation cycles yield field-specific422 errors. A new project key must be unused.

Every included ID is regenerated. Parent/label/status/comment/relation references are explicitly remapped; original issue numbers (including deletion gaps), board ranks, estimates, due dates, descriptions, authors and createdAt/updatedAt survive. next_issue_number becomes maximum imported number+1, independent of export ordering. User mappings may name only current non-guest destination organization members; absent mappings resolve an exported catalog email by exact normalized email lookup, never by trusting an arbitrary foreign ID. Explicit user remapping updates canonical user mention IDs. External relation endpoints require explicit externalIssueMap entries pointing to writable existing issues in the same organization. Their relations may affect those existing issues.

Validation precedes a single synchronous outer transaction. Import reuses canonical createIssue/createComment/createRelation services through a staged transaction/event context; events are published from refreshed canonical readers only after successful commit. A validation or write failure leaves no project or index/activity/notification effects. Workflow/label encoding reuses the existing work schemas and public readers. Browser transfer requires a successful current preview and confirmation before creation, retains file/form/mappings on errors, and exposes result counts/project link. Current shared JSON request limit is2MiB.

crew export PROJECT [--format json|csv] [--output NEW_FILE] streams stdout or creates a private new file, reports bytes/SHA256 and refuses overwrite. crew import --org ID --file EXPORT.json --key NEWKEY [--name NAME] [--user-map MAP.json] [--external-map MAP.json] --preview|--yes streams the document with explicit metadata. Mapping files contain exported-ID to destination-ID objects. Every import is revalidated on the server; preview does not reserve a key.

## Activity and inbox CLI

crew feed list --org ID supports --project, --issue, --user, --entity, --action, --from, --to, --limit, --cursor and --all. crew feed subscriptions --org ID lists owned watches; crew feed watch|unwatch issue|project ID changes only the caller's watch. crew inbox list --org ID supports --project,--state all|unread|read and pagination. read|unread ID changes one item; mark --ids ID,ID and mark-all --org ID --yes support --read true|false. preferences --org ID [--email true|false] [--mentions-only true|false] reads/updates preferences. digest --org ID queues one batch; digests --org ID lists authorized digest views. Every group supports credential-free --help.

## Authorized selectors and scoped UI state

GET /insight/options accepts type=organizations|projects|issues|users, orgId for all except organizations, optional projectId, q, id, permission, limit and cursor. It always requires insight:read, plus org:read for organization/user catalogs and a fixed project read boundary. The permission context may further require project:read,export:read or issue:write and can never weaken the fixed minimum. Current role/project access is filtered before matching, totals and cursors. User choices are current non-guest organization members for import authorship; current people roster permissions remain required. id resolves an authorized selected choice outside the current search page. EntityPicker provides native keyboard selection, a search box, explicit Previous/Next pages and readable selected identities. Later pages remain reachable in organizations, projects and issue watches.

Inbox watch lookup displays current manual/automatic watch state and readable target names. Watch, digest and preference panels reset their cursor/action lifetimes when the organization changes. Scoped loading hides previous organization/filter data and errors immediately, while request-generation guards reject responses belonging to a replaced file, key, mapping or organization. Transfer selects clear the old document before every new file check, including oversized/invalid files. A current successful preview plus confirmation authorizes only that draft; import controls remain fixed while its request is in flight. Every included record catalog and resolved mapping has bounded searchable pages, with full text available on demand.

Dashboard current-work filters are statusId,assigneeId (or unassigned),priority=0..4 and overdue=true|false; issueCursor/issueLimit paginate the matching canonical issue table. Chart groups are keyboard actionable and filter the current set. Current-work filters do not filter historical throughput or the canonical sprint ledger; project scope and ending date determine the completion history. Charts expose underlying tables and bounded searchable group pages.

Insight watch/read/preference/digest mutations emit owned domain events. Private inbox SSE frames contain only safe action/identity metadata, are delivered to the exact current credential owner and current project grants, and never enter general activity. Reconnection refreshes a live view to reconcile any missed private events. Cleanup closes both public and private live delivery.
